Clinical details: Severe aortic stenosis, LVEF 45%. Current smoker. TAVI work-up.

Technique: ECG-gated CT angiography of the aortic root and heart, followed by non-gated CT angiography from the thoracic inlet to the lesser trochanters. 70 ml iohexol 350. DLP 655 mGy·cm.

Findings:

Thoracic aorta: Ascending aorta 39 mm. Arch and descending thoracic aorta of normal calibre. No dissection.

Subclavian/axillary arteries: Unremarkable. No significant stenosis.

Abdominal aorta: Normal calibre. No abdominal aortic aneurysm. Coeliac axis, SMA and renal arteries patent.

Iliofemoral access (minimal luminal diameter):
Right: CIA 7.2 mm, EIA 6.3 mm, CFA 6.9 mm.
Left: CIA 7.5 mm, EIA 6.2 mm, CFA 6.6 mm.
Calcification: moderate, non-circumferential. Tortuosity: moderate. No dissection or flow-limiting stenosis.

Lungs and airways: 9 mm solid nodule in the left lower lobe with a lobulated margin (series 5, image 241); Brock risk 16%. No other pulmonary nodule. Moderate centrilobular emphysema. No consolidation. Airways patent. Surveillance per BTS guidance is appropriate only if the patient would be fit for further investigation or treatment; for consideration by the referring team.

Pleura and pericardium: No pleural or pericardial effusion.

Mediastinum: No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.

Upper abdomen: Simple left renal cyst. Otherwise unremarkable within the limits of an arterial phase study.

Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion. Mild thoracic kyphosis.

Conclusion:
1. Iliofemoral access favourable for a transfemoral approach bilaterally; minimal luminal diameter right 6.3 mm, left 6.2 mm.
2. 9 mm lobulated left lower lobe nodule, Brock risk 16%. Discussion at the lung cancer MDT is suggested if a diagnosis would alter management.

Annular sizing, valve morphology, coronary ostial heights and aortic root measurements are reported separately in the structural heart report; please refer to that report for valve planning.
